key_insight: Aligned MAPbI3 nanowalls reveal that ferroelastic symmetry breaking can split excitons in a polarization-selective way and evolve them into lattice-coupled states across the phase transition.
engineering_relevance: This suggests crystal texture and phase control can be used to engineer anisotropic optical response in perovskite devices, relevant for next-generation light-harvesting and photonic architectures.
method: Glancing-angle deposition to fabricate highly aligned MAPbI3 nanowalls with a defined optical axis
Temperature-dependent photoluminescence and X-ray diffraction to track phase evolution
Polarization-resolved ultrafast transient absorption to resolve excitonic splitting and coupling
evidence_signal: The abstract reports orthogonal optical selection rules with a 45 meV excitonic splitting at 5 K and a 58 meV lower-energy lattice-coupled feature near 160 K.
watch_item: The symmetry-dependent effects were demonstrated on specialized nanowall structures, so transferability to typical polycrystalline perovskite films may be limited.
paper_title: Ferroelastic exciton splitting in hybrid perovskite nanowalls
